title: Token-rate profiling orchestrator for cross-model benchmarking
creator: Ava Chen
description: Build an orchestrator and test harness that runs repeatable tokens-per-second (TPS) profiles across core models, hardware families, and workload shapes. The orchestrator should produce reproducible artifacts (raw traces, latency histograms, token throughput time series) and support automated regression detection integrated into our CI and monitoring pipelines.
background: We have many one-off microbenchmarks for throughput and p95 but lack a unified, reproducible orchestrator that can compare hardware (A100/RTX/Graviton), quantization variants, and warm vs cold KV cache conditions. This makes cross-model regressions noisy and slow to triage. Prior tickets focused on microbench harnesses and TPS probes, but gaps remain in statistical regression testing and artifact retention for audits.
proposed_solution: Implement a scheduler-style orchestrator that: 1) generates workload profiles (seq lengths, prompt prefixes, temperature/beam variants); 2) runs N independent trials per configuration; 3) captures per-token latency and GPU metrics; 4) computes robust summary stats (median TPS, p95 latency, inter-run variance, bootstrapped confidence intervals); 5) runs regression tests using control charts and non-parametric hypothesis tests; 6) stores artifacts to s3 with immutable run IDs; 7) exposes metadata and summary CSVs to the Console and CI. Provide a minimal CLI and REST interface for ad-hoc runs.
success_metrics: Can reproduce median TPS within 5% across independent runs for the same config
p95 latency drift detection sensitivity: identify 10% regression with >90% recall in CI
Artifacts retained and indexed for 90 days in s3 for audit
Integration with CI: blocking PRs when a trained baseline regression is detected
Run-to-run variance documented per model and hardware (target CV < 12% for steady-state workloads)
acceptance_criteria: Orchestrator can execute predefined matrix of (model, hardware, quant, seq_len) and produce raw traces and summary CSV
Statistical regression test runs in < 10m for a standard baseline matrix and returns PASS/FAIL
CI job plugs into existing pipeline and blocks when regression detection triggers
Dashboards show run comparisons with embedded artifact links and downloadable histograms
Playbook documented for investigating a failing regression (triage steps, flame graphs, suggested mitigations)
tasks: Design storage schema and run metadata format (immutable run_id, tags, artifact pointers)
Implement run scheduler and worker harness (CLI + simple REST API)
Instrument per-token latency capture and GPU telemetry exporters
Implement statistical analysis module (bootstrap CIs, Mann–Whitney U test, control charts)
Integrate with s3 artifact storage and indexer for Console
Add CI integration: lightweight baseline job and gating logic
Create Console dashboard panels and links to raw artifacts
Author docs and runbook for oncall and SRE teams
risks: Hardware noise causing false positives — mitigated by requiring N independent trials and bootstrapping
Long run times for large matrices — mitigated by parallelism and sampling strategies
Too-sensitive statistical tests flagging benign drift — mitigate by configurable thresholds and baseline windows
Storage costs for raw traces — mitigate with configurable retention and compression policies
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (internal alpha): small matrix (3 models x 2 hardware types x 2 seq_lengths), store artifacts to dev s3, manual inspection. Phase 2 (beta): expand matrix, add CI job, enable non-blocking alerts in Console. Phase 3 (GA): gating CI policy enabled for selected runtime releases and model families; run retention policy enforced.
ci_integration: Provide a lightweight GitHub Actions job template and Jenkins pipeline snippet that downloads the latest baseline, runs the orchestrator matrix in a controlled environment, uploads artifacts, and evaluates regression tests. Failures emit a annotated status with links to artifacts and suggested bisect steps.
